sections.heading: Song history
sections.wikitext:
Jon Bon Jovi did not like the original recording of this song, which is present as a [[hidden track]] on ''[[100,000,000 Bon Jovi Fans Can't Be Wrong]]''. Lead guitarist Richie Sambora, however, convinced him the song was good, and they reworked it with a new bassline (recorded by [[Hugh McDonald (American musician)|Hugh McDonald]] uncredited<ref name="On Bass: The Song Guys">{{cite web|last=Brodén|first=Victor|title=On Bass: The Song Guys|url=https://www.premierguitar.com/articles/21155-on-bass-the-song-guys|website=Premier Guitar|date=July 23, 2014|access-date=March 10, 2017|language=en|archive-date=June 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143446/https://www.premierguitar.com/articles/21155-on-bass-the-song-guys|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="forbes.com">{{cite web|last=Setaro|first=Shawn|title=Inside The Business Of Bon Jovi With Bryan Reesman|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/shawnsetaro/2016/10/26/business-bon-jovi-bryan-reesman/#21f9a6ea381b|website=Forbes|access-date=March 11, 2017|archive-date=March 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312085534/https://www.forbes.com/sites/shawnsetaro/2016/10/26/business-bon-jovi-bryan-reesman/#21f9a6ea381b|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=McDonald |first=Hugh |title=Hugh McDonald Official Website – Discography |url=http://www.huey-mcdonald.com/discography.php |website=Internet Archive |access-date=March 11, 2017 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120302012105/http://www.huey-mcdonald.com/discography.php |archive-date=March 2, 2012 }}</ref>), different drum fills and the use of a [[talk box]] to include it on ''Slippery When Wet''. The song spent two weeks at number one on the [[Mainstream Rock Tracks]] chart, from January 31 to February 14, 1987, and four weeks at number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100, from February 14 to March 14. It also hit number four on the [[UK Singles Chart]].

The album version, timed around 4:10, fades out at the end. However, the music video game ''[[Guitar Hero World Tour]]'' features the song's original studio ending, where the band revisit the intro riff and end with a talk box solo; this version ends at 4:53. The original ending is also playable on the similar video game ''[[Rock Band 2]]'', though edited in this case (thereby eliminating the talk box solo at the end). The version included on the 2005 [[DualDisc]] edition of ''Slippery When Wet'' has an extended version of the original ending, with a different talk box solo playing over the riff (possibly taken from an outtake of the song); this version, which fades out at the end like the standard version of the song, ends at 5:06.

Bon Jovi recorded an alternative version, "Prayer 94", for the 1994 greatest-hits album ''[[Cross Road (album)|Cross Road]]''. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' named it one of "seven pop music remakes that never should have happened", criticizing its alteration of the song's "greatest strength", its chorus melody, and speculating that it was "a play for respectability" after the rise of [[grunge]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Modell |first=Josh |date=May 2, 2018 |title=7 Pop music remakes that never should've happened |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/7-pop-music-remakes-that-never-shouldve-happened-630356/bon-jovi-prayer-94-630363/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=April 8, 2025}}</ref>

After the [[September 11, 2001 attacks]] – in which New Jersey was the second-hardest hit state after New York, suffering hundreds of casualties among both [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|WTC]] workers and [[first responders]] – the band performed an acoustic version of this song for New York. Bon Jovi performed a similar version as part of the special ''[[America: A Tribute to Heroes]]''.

In 2022, [[Mike Reno]], vocalist of the band [[Loverboy]], said he was certain the backing vocals he recorded for this song are used.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://loudwire.com/loverboy-mike-reno-reveals-backing-vocal-bon-jovi-livin-on-a-prayer/|title = Loverboy's Mike Reno Reveals Backing Vocal on Bon Jovi's 'Livin' on a Prayer'|website = [[Loudwire]]|date = February 9, 2022|access-date = February 20, 2022|archive-date = October 7, 2023|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20231007000054/https://loudwire.com/loverboy-mike-reno-reveals-backing-vocal-bon-jovi-livin-on-a-prayer/|url-status = live}}</ref>

Jon Bon Jovi did not like the original recording of this song, which is present as a hidden track on 100,000,000 Bon Jovi Fans Can't Be Wrong. Lead guitarist Richie Sambora, however, convinced him the song was good, and they reworked it with a new bassline (recorded by Hugh McDonald uncredited), different drum fills and the use of a talk box to include it on Slippery When Wet. The song spent two weeks at number one on the Mainstream Rock Tracks chart, from January 31 to February 14, 1987, and four weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, from February 14 to March 14. It also hit number four on the UK Singles Chart.

The album version, timed around 4:10, fades out at the end. However, the music video game Guitar Hero World Tour features the song's original studio ending, where the band revisit the intro riff and end with a talk box solo; this version ends at 4:53. The original ending is also playable on the similar video game Rock Band 2, though edited in this case (thereby eliminating the talk box solo at the end). The version included on the 2005 DualDisc edition of Slippery When Wet has an extended version of the original ending, with a different talk box solo playing over the riff (possibly taken from an outtake of the song); this version, which fades out at the end like the standard version of the song, ends at 5:06.

Bon Jovi recorded an alternative version, "Prayer 94", for the 1994 greatest-hits album Cross Road. Rolling Stone named it one of "seven pop music remakes that never should have happened", criticizing its alteration of the song's "greatest strength", its chorus melody, and speculating that it was "a play for respectability" after the rise of grunge.

After the September 11, 2001 attacks – in which New Jersey was the second-hardest hit state after New York, suffering hundreds of casualties among both WTC workers and first responders – the band performed an acoustic version of this song for New York. Bon Jovi performed a similar version as part of the special America: A Tribute to Heroes.

In 2022, Mike Reno, vocalist of the band Loverboy, said he was certain the backing vocals he recorded for this song are used.

sections.heading: Reception and legacy
sections.wikitext:
''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' said that "metal muscle meets gritty reality in a tough, clanging rocker."<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=Billboard|date=December 13, 1986|accessdate=August 7, 2022|page=61|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ICUEAAAAMBAJ&q=reviews|title=Reviews}}</ref>  ''[[Cash Box]]'' said that "Solid chorus and ringing guitar highlight Jon Bon Jovi’s gutsy singing."<ref name=cb>{{cite magazine|title=Single Releases|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/80s/1986/CB-1986-12-13.pdf|magazine=Cash Box|date=December 13, 1986|accessdate=August 7, 2022|page=8|archive-date=May 19, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519094718/https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/80s/1986/CB-1986-12-13.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2006, online voters rated "Livin' on a Prayer" No. 1 on [[VH1]]'s list of The 100 Greatest Songs of the '80s. More recently, in New Zealand, "Livin' on a Prayer" was No. 1 on the [[C4 (New Zealand)|C4]] music channel's show ''[[U Choose 40]]'', on the 80's Icons list. It was also No. 1 on the "Sing-a-long Classics List". After Bon Jovi performed in New Zealand on January 28, 2008, while on their [[Lost Highway Tour]], the song re-entered the official New Zealand [[RIANZ]] singles chart at number 24, over twenty years after the initial release.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rianz.org.nz/rianz/chart.asp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110317025609/http://www.rianz.org.nz/rianz/chart.asp|url-status=dead|title=RIANZ|archive-date=March 17, 2011|access-date=January 4, 2020}}</ref>

Australian music TV channel [[MAX (Australian TV channel)|MAX]] placed the song at No. 18 on their 2008 countdown "Rock Songs: Top 100". In 2009, the song returned to the charts in the UK, notably hitting the number-one spot on the [[UK Rock Chart]].

In 2010, it was chosen in an online vote on the Grammy.com website over the group's more recent hits "[[Always (Bon Jovi song)|Always]]" and "[[It's My Life (Bon Jovi song)|It's My Life]]" to be played live by the band on the [[52nd Grammy Awards]] telecast.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.grammy.com/news/more-grammy-performers-presenters-announced|title=More GRAMMY Performers, Presenters Announced|date=April 30, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2010|archive-date=January 31, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100131120752/http://www.grammy.com/news/more-grammy-performers-presenters-announced|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/dailynews/columnists/jonathan_takiff/20100201_BEYONCE_SWIFT_BOATED.html|title=Beyonce Swift Boated|access-date=February 2, 2010|archive-date=February 5, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100205081033/http://www.philly.com/dailynews/columnists/jonathan_takiff/20100201_BEYONCE_SWIFT_BOATED.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 50th Anniversary list, "Livin' on a Prayer" was named the 46th greatest rock song of all time.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top-rock.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080913205910/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top-rock.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=September In November 2013, the song made its return to the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 at number 25, due to a [[viral video]].

In 2017, [[ShortList]]'s Dave Fawbert listed the song as containing "one of the greatest [[Modulation (music)|key changes]] in music history".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.shortlist.com/entertainment/music/the-best-key-changes-music/329120|title=The 19 greatest key changes in music history|magazine=[[ShortList]]|date=October 1, 2017|access-date=January 13, 2018|archive-date=January 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180114073845/https://www.shortlist.com/entertainment/music/the-best-key-changes-music/329120|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2015, "Sleazegrinder" of ''[[Louder (website)|Louder]]'' included the song in his list of "The 20 Greatest Hair Metal Anthems Of All Time", placing it at number 12.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sleazegrinder |date=December 4, 2015 |title=The 20 Best Hair Metal Anthems Of All Time Ever |url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/the-best-20-hair-metal-anthems-of-all-time-ever |website=Louder |access-date=December 21, 2025}}</ref>

In 2021, ''Rolling Stone'' ranked the song at number 457 in their updated list of the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|500 Greatest Songs of All Time]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=September 15, 2021 |title=The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-of-all-time-1224767/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |access-date=June 9, 2022 |archive-date=September 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915162053/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-of-all-time-1224767/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2010, it was chosen in an online vote on the Grammy.com website over the group's more recent hits "Always" and "It's My Life" to be played live by the band on the 52nd Grammy Awards telecast.

sections.heading: Lyrics
sections.wikitext:
The song describes two characters, Tommy and Gina, a working-class couple who struggle to make ends meet. Tommy loses his job as a dockworker due to a strike while Gina works as a diner waitress. Its storyline was loosely based on real-life events that Richie Sambora, Jon Bon Jovi and songwriter Desmond Child witnessed and experienced in the 1970s. The 1977 Dockworkers' Strike was the inspiration for Tommy's plight, in which the [[International Longshoremen's Association]] (ILA) engaged in a seven-week work stoppage. In another case, before becoming successful artists and songwriters, Desmond Child and his then-girlfriend, singer-songwriter [[Maria Vidal]], lived together and had already begun their music careers, while still working day jobs; Child was a taxi driver in New York while Vidal was employed as a waitress in a diner named "Once Upon A Stove", similar to Gina in the song. The owner, manager, and other employees of the diner nicknamed Vidal "Gina" due to her slight physical resemblance to Italian actress and photographer [[Gina Lollobrigida]].

"It deals with the way that two kids – Tommy and Gina – face life's struggles," noted Bon Jovi, "and how their love and ambitions get them through the hard times. It's working class and it's real… I wanted to incorporate the movie element, and tell a story about people I knew. So instead of doing what I did on '[[Runaway (Bon Jovi song)|Runaway]]', where the girl didn't have a name, I gave them names, which gave them an identity... Tommy and Gina aren't two specific people; they represent a lifestyle."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Malcolm|last=Dome|author-link=Malcolm Dome|title=We'll make it, I swear…|magazine=[[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]] |issue=94|date=July 2006|pages=45–46}}</ref> Tommy and Gina are also referred to in Bon Jovi's 1988 song "[[New Jersey (album)|99 in the Shade]]" and their 2000 single "[[It's My Life (Bon Jovi song)|It's My Life]]".

In a 2002 interview, Bon Jovi said that he wrote the song as a response to the [[Reagan Era]], adding, "[[trickle-down economics]] are really inspirational to writing songs".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://top40-charts.com/news.php?nid=4226&string=George|title=Bon Jovi Calls George Bush as 'lunatcic'!|website=Top40-Charts.com}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The music video was filmed on September 17, 1986, at the [[Grand Olympic Auditorium]] in Los Angeles, California and was directed by [[Wayne Isham]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mvdbase.com/tech.php?last=Isham&first=Wayne|title=mvdbase.com – Wayne Isham technician videography|access-date=May 31, 2010|archive-date=January 5, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105010814/http://mvdbase.com/tech.php?last=Isham&first=Wayne|url-status=live}}</ref> It starts with a silhouette of the band walking down a hall, followed by shots of the band rehearsing, filmed in black and white, then playing in front of a crowd, in color. Near the beginning of the song, Jon puts on a harness that is being attached to wires by professional stunt coordinators and stunt spotters, and during the final chorus, he soars over the crowd.

The video reached 1 billion views on YouTube (the band's second song to do so) on February 1, 2023.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Rowley |first1=Glenn |date=January 2, 2023 |title=Bon Jovi's 'Livin' On a Prayer' Video Joins YouTube's Billion-Views Club |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/bon-jovi-livin-on-a-prayer-video-youtube-billion-views-club-1235209587/ |magazine=Billboard |access-date=March 22, 2024 |archive-date=March 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240322024005/https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/bon-jovi-livin-on-a-prayer-video-youtube-billion-views-club-1235209587/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

sections.heading: Alternative versions
sections.wikitext:
In the [[1989 MTV Video Music Awards]], Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora performed acoustic versions of this song and "[[Wanted Dead or Alive (Bon Jovi song)|Wanted Dead or Alive]]". While [[MTV Unplugged]] was already in development by the time of this event, its [[showrunners]] have credited the pair's performance with influencing the show to go from initially being meant only for "young, up-and-coming artists" into being a simplified showcase for the "big, stadium, electric-arena-type acts".<ref>{{cite web |last=Harvilla |first=Rob |date=September 7, 2017 |title=Nirvana, Lauryn Hill, and Faxes From Don Henley: Behind the Scenes at the Original 'MTV Unplugged' |url=https://www.theringer.com/2017/09/07/music/mtv-unplugged-nirvana-don-henley-paul-mccartney |work=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] |access-date=April 15, 2025}}</ref>

A re-recorded and slower version of the song, "Prayer '94," also appeared on U.S. versions of the band's ''[[Cross Road (album)|Cross Road]]'' hits collection.<ref>{{Cite AV media notes |id=P2-26013 |publisher=[[Mercury Records]] |title=[[Cross Road (album)|Cross Road]] |others=[[Bon Jovi]] |year=1994 |type=liner notes}}</ref>

A parody of the song<ref>{{cite news|url=https://people.com/super-bowl-2026-jon-bon-jovi-stars-in-first-ever-big-game-commercial-exclusive-11900423|title='Livin' on a Prayer' parody, Hailee Steinfeld in State Farm Super Bowl ad)|work=[[USA Today]]|date=February 8, 2026|access-date=February 9, 2026}}</ref> was used in a 2026 [[Super Bowl commercial]] for [[State Farm Insurance]]. Jon Bon Jovi appears in the commercial called "Stop Livin' on a Prayer".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://people.com/super-bowl-2026-jon-bon-jovi-stars-in-first-ever-big-game-commercial-exclusive-11900423|title=Jon Bon Jovi Is the Real Deal and Wants You to Stop 'Livin' on a Prayer' in Super Bowl Commercial for State Farm (Exclusive)|last=Sengwe|first=Stephanie|work=[[People (magazine)|People]]|date=February 8, 2026|access-date=February 9, 2026}}</ref>
sections.text:
In the 1989 MTV Video Music Awards, Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora performed acoustic versions of this song and "Wanted Dead or Alive". While MTV Unplugged was already in development by the time of this event, its showrunners have credited the pair's performance with influencing the show to go from initially being meant only for "young, up-and-coming artists" into being a simplified showcase for the "big, stadium, electric-arena-type acts".

A re-recorded and slower version of the song, "Prayer '94," also appeared on U.S. versions of the band's Cross Road hits collection.

A parody of the song was used in a 2026 Super Bowl commercial for State Farm Insurance. Jon Bon Jovi appears in the commercial called "Stop Livin' on a Prayer".
